source.test: exportServerTransfer(to:) + applyTransferImport(...) — paper.jar missing on disk

expected.no_log_message_for_missing_jar: fm.fileExists(atPath: jarURL.path) guards the copy attempt (source line 158); when it's false the whole `do`/`catch` block is skipped, so no [Transfer] log line is emitted -- the failure log at line 163 only fires if fileExists is true but copyItem itself throws.

apply_time_paper_jar_path.reasoning: applyTransferImport only looks for a package's paper.jar when entry.bundledPaperJar is true (source line 440's `if entry.server.isJava && entry.bundledPaperJar`); since export recorded bundledPaperJar: false, apply never checks the staging dir for a jar at all, and cfgServer.paperJarPath stays the empty string set at line 439 -- even if a paper.jar happened to be dropped into the package's server folder by hand after export, apply would not pick it up.

notes: Distinguishes 'jar legitimately doesn't apply to this flavor' (forge-libraries-bundled.json) from 'jar was expected but is absent' -- same bundledPaperJar: false wire value, but reached by a different branch, and this fixture also pins the apply-side symmetry (bundledPaperJar gates the *read*, not just the export).
